findings.description: The proposed tests contain a streak-counting ambiguity: F001 says clearance_streak counts consecutive full-clearance rounds ending at the latest round, but F003 expects C0 round 3 to have streak=2 while rounds 1-2 are not eligible despite the stated 100% clearance across rounds 1-3.

The plan does not explicitly require the full completion-path test where an eligible high matrix_pin refusal is followed by recording waived_matrix_pin_high and then the same lock succeeds without any paid auditor invocation.

The fallback_blocked journey state is named in the objective, and F001 mentions conservative-fallback findings, but F003 only calls out plan_contract discrimination fixtures and does not require a concrete fallback-classed or unclassified high blocker case.

F002 asks the refusal output to name the exact disposition command, but also forbids default confirmation text anywhere in the path. That leaves the CLI contract under-specified and risks either a non-runnable command or an accidental canned confirmation.

The proposed end-to-end completion path is not satisfiable against the real C0 round-3 ledger as written: that round contains an eligible high matrix_pin, but it also contains a medium plan_contract finding and other medium blockers. Recording only waived_matrix_pin_high cannot both permit the lock and preserve the rule that plan_contract findings remain blocked regardless of streak.

The objective lists auditor prompt changes as a non-goal, but the proposed features do not require any scope guard proving the sufficiency auditor prompt, schema contract, or classifier instructions stay unchanged while adding the v1.1 policy and fixture replay.

F001 says plan_contract classifications remain absolute blocks, while F003 relies on an existing medium plan_contract being neutralized by waived_with_reason. That wording can drive an implementation that blocks the completion-path fixture despite the stated non-goal of changing medium handling.

F001 introduces a configurable streak threshold N, but the plan does not explicitly pin one shared threshold source across convergence_verdict, lock-refusal messaging, and record_disposition validation. A split default would create eligible-looking refusals that the disposition command later rejects, or the reverse.

The proposed tests cover unlocked eligibility and fallback refusal strongly, but the no_streak_blocked and critical_blocked user-facing states are only indirectly covered by helper or matrix expectations. The lock refusal surface should be pinned for those states because it is part of the operator journey.

F001 says plan_contract findings remain absolute blocks, but later acceptance text and F003 rely on unchanged v1 behavior where plan_contract can be neutralized by waived_with_reason or a plan edit. That wording can lead implementers to make plan_contract unwaivable, breaking the stated completion path.

The objective completion test says recording waived_matrix_pin_high with confirmation text then permits the lock, but F003's real C0 path only permits after every other blocker is also dispositioned and separately asserts that recording only the matrix-pin waiver still refuses. The plan does not directly prove the new disposition can be the final gate to lock success.

F003 says only the real sufficiency-rounds ledgers are copied verbatim, but one discrimination assertion depends on C0 round 4 having its matrix_pin high already dispositioned. If dispositions live in decisions.jsonl, the fixture plan needs that decision history or an explicit test setup step.

The user journey names no_streak_blocked as a core state, but the proposed refusal-message coverage focuses on the streak-unlocked case. C0 rounds 1 and 2 are asserted not eligible, yet there is no explicit lock-refusal assertion that the runnable waiver command is withheld below the threshold.
